I ran `/code-conventions --review-pr` over `a8ca1696a…HEAD`. That range is one commit, `61942e764 feat: migrate HTTP platform from Express to Fastify`, touching 121 files. I went through all 60 rules in the generated checklist. I wrote the checklist to my scratchpad instead of `docs/engineering/`, so no tracked files changed. I didn't need to look up the history behind any rule, and I didn't run tests or install dependencies.

**Rules that applied:** CHANGE-03, CHANGE-04, PR-01, PR-02, MOD-04, REUSE-01, STYLE-01, TYPE-06, CONFIG-04, TEST-02 and TEST-09. The PR passes all the others that bear on it: every changed file has its SPDX header, the `EXPRESS_*` env var names are kept so existing deployments still work, and the auth guards and space routes behave as before.

**Checked and cleared:**
- Form-encoded bodies on `POST /v1/auth/logout/redirect` still work: `@nestjs/platform-fastify` ships `@fastify/formbody` (yarn.lock:1788).
- The new `@fastify/static` dependency is a required peer of `@nestjs/serve-static` (yarn.lock:1863).
- Cookie `maxAge` moved correctly from milliseconds (Express) to seconds (Fastify) through `getSecondsUntil`, and the specs were updated to match.

## Findings

| # | Rule | Location | Finding |
|---|------|----------|---------|
| 1 | CONFIG-04 | `package.json:49-50` | `"@fastify/cookie": "^11.0.2"` and `"@fastify/static": "^9.1.3"` use caret ranges. The rule wants runtime dependencies pinned exactly, and the packages bumped alongside them in this PR are exact (`@nestjs/platform-fastify: "11.1.24"`). `@fastify/cookie` handles the auth cookie. |
| 2 | PR-02 / CHANGE-03 | `src/config/entities/configuration.ts:383-393`, `.env.sample.json:622` | The docs still describe the Express behaviour: the limit is "passed to the bytes library", it "defaults to '100kb'", and links go to expressjs.com. Now the local `parseBodyLimit` parses it, accepting only `b/kb/mb/gb` where `bytes` also took `tb`/`pb`. Fastify's `bodyLimit` also covers every content type, not just JSON. The config keys can keep their `express.*` names for compatibility (CHANGE-04), but the comments and sample descriptions should match what runs now. |
| 3 | STYLE-01 / PR-01 | `src/routes/common/http/http-request.utils.ts:8-9, 18-22, 40-41, 53-54`; `src/logging/utils.ts:43` | `RequestLike` and its helpers keep fallbacks that only Express requests use: `header()`, `get()`, `route.path`, `path`. With Express removed, these branches can't run for a `FastifyRequest`. `request.method ?? 'UNKNOWN'` is also dead, because Fastify always sets `method`. The rule asks for no dead branches. Typing the helpers against `FastifyRequest` (plus `originalUrl` for the middleware) would remove about half the file. |
| 4 | MOD-04 / PR-01 | `src/app.provider.ts:34, 38, 69`; `src/main.ts:15` | `parseTrustProxy` and `parseBodyLimit` are exported but only used inside the file (MOD-04: don't export symbols nobody imports). `createFastifyAdapter` is a production export used only by tests (`test-app.provider.ts:57`, `app.provider.spec.ts:46`). Meanwhile `main.ts` builds its adapter from the raw `configuration()` output, not from `IConfigurationService`. So production and tests take two different routes to the same settings, and the one the spec tests is not the one production uses. |
| 5 | TEST-09 / TEST-02 | `src/app.provider.ts:34-56`, `src/app.provider.spec.ts:97` | `parseBodyLimit` has several branches: undefined → default, a plain integer, decimal-with-unit values like `1.5mb`, and invalid input → throw. Its only coverage is one 413 case that starts up the whole Nest app. These are pure functions, so plain unit tests are the right place for the edge cases, especially the throw, which is what makes a bad config fail at startup. `parseTrustProxy` has no direct test of the numeric-vs-string split either. |
| 6 | TYPE-06 / REUSE-01 | `src/__tests__/test-app.provider.ts:17-20` | `createTestApplication` casts `module.createNestApplication(new FastifyAdapter()) as NestFastifyApplication`, but the method takes a generic, which `provide()` at line 55 already uses. The helper also builds a bare adapter with no `trustProxy` or `bodyLimit`, so 15 specs use it and 67 use `TestAppProvider`. There are now two ways to create a test app, and they set the adapter up differently. |
| 7 | REUSE-01 | `src/modules/auth/utils/auth-cookie.utils.ts:3-9` | A local `CookieOptions` type replaces the old import from express. `@fastify/cookie`, which the code now calls through `res.setCookie`, already exports its options type (`CookieSerializeOptions`). Reusing it keeps the options type in step with the library if the library changes. |
| 8 | STYLE-01 | `src/app.provider.ts:34-76`; `src/app.provider.spec.ts:~71, ~91` | The removed `configureTrustProxy` had JSDoc explaining hop count vs subnet list, with a link. The new public functions that took over (`parseTrustProxy`, `createFastifyAdapter*`) have no doc at all. The spec also lost its comments on the right-to-left `X-Forwarded-For` walk, even though that behaviour is unchanged and security-relevant. |

Findings 1–4 have the most effect. 5–8 are smaller cleanups. There were no rule failures I couldn't decide and no open questions.
